steps.procedure: 1. Release the pressure that remains in the hydraulic tank and piping to examine. For details, see Testing and Adjusting, “Release Remained Pressure in Hydraulic Circuit”. 2. Examine the control valve body and the boom spool to see if they are not twisted or stuck and that they do not have any damage or dirt on them. (They must move smoothly and not be stuck.) REMARK Be careful that dirt does not enter during recovery work.

branches.YES: • Bucket control valve body and spool are normal. • Go to the next check item.
branches.NO: • Bucket control valve body and spool are defective. • Repair or replace the bucket control valve body and spool. • Go to “Confirmation of repair”.

steps.cause: Pressure compensation valve on IN side of bucket control valve
steps.procedure: 1. Examine it. For details, see Testing and Adjusting, “Examine and Adjust Oil Pressure in Work Equipment, Swing, and Travel Circuits”. 2. Does the troubleshooting result of the main relief pressure agree with the judgment criteria? 3. Do relief of other work equipment and examine. 4. Is the bucket stopped? 5. Interchange the pressure compensation valves on IN and OUT sides of bucket control valve, and examine. 6. Is there no change, and does the phenomenon reproduce? REMARK The area ratios of the pressure compensation valves on the IN side and OUT sides are different. Be sure to set them back to their initial positions after troubleshooting.
